issues.description: The script sends latitude and longitude coordinates to the third-party service nominatim.openstreetmap.org via GM_xmlhttpRequest for reverse geocoding.
issues.recommendation: Ensure only non-sensitive, non-personal data is sent. Inform users of this external request. Consider proxying or limiting data exposure.

issues.description: The script requests Notification API permissions and can send browser notifications.
issues.recommendation: Ensure notifications are not abused. Inform users about notification usage.

issues.description: The script applies Proxy wrappers to native functions (e.g., setAttribute, push, fetch) to bypass anti-cheat and tracking mechanisms. This is advanced behavior that could be abused for obfuscation or evasion.
issues.recommendation: Review all Proxy usage for legitimate purpose. Avoid using Proxies to hide malicious behavior.

issues.description: The script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest permission and @connect for discord.com, but no code in the provided snippet sends data to discord.com. This is a potential over-privilege.
issues.recommendation: Remove unused permissions to reduce attack surface.

issues.description: The script modifies frame sandboxing behavior by disabling the 'sandbox' attribute on iframes for certain platforms, which may weaken clickjacking protections.
issues.recommendation: Do not remove or bypass iframe sandboxing unless absolutely necessary and safe.

script_name: CheatGuessr Universal | GeoGuessr | OpenGuessr | WorldGuessr | FreeGuessr
summary: This script transmits user location data (latitude/longitude) to a third-party geocoding service (nominatim.openstreetmap.org), which is a critical data exfiltration risk. It also requests notification permissions, modifies native browser APIs via Proxy (which could be abused for evasion or obfuscation), and requests more permissions than it uses. There is no evidence of direct privacy collection (e.g., cookies, input fields), DOM XSS, or supply chain risk in the provided code. The overall risk is HIGH due to the external data transmission and advanced API manipulation. User consent and transparency are recommended. Remove unused permissions and avoid weakening browser security features.
